entities.summary: Alfonso de Valdés was a Spanish humanist born in 1490 in Cuenca who worked at the chancellery of the Emperor Charles V and served as the twin brother of Juan de Valdés. He played a crucial role in the development of the Compendio de las Historias, a comprehensive history of Spain that would become a foundational text for future historians. Through his work, de Valdés contributed to the shaping of the Spanish Empire's early historical narratives and influenced the development of humanist scholarship in the 16th century. His legacy extended to the creation of the Historia de España, a multi-volume work that chronicled the history of Spain from the Roman Empire to the early modern period. De Valdés' contributions to historical scholarship had a lasting impact on the field, and his work remains an important resource for historians studying the early modern period in Spain.
